$comment: Reviewer registry for this repository — a port of dotfiles/harness/review-attestation.json,
trimmed to the reviewers that measurably act here. Precedent for a per-repo port: kubelab,
hive, web and ts-bridge each carry their own copy; the SSOT of the SHAPE stays in dotfiles.
Why the port was needed: this file did not exist, so `dotf pr triage-queue` could not answer
at all — `read reviewer registry: open harness/review-attestation.json: no such file or
directory`. Its exit status is 1 both when triage is pending AND when the question cannot be
computed, precisely so an unanswerable queue is never mistaken for a clear one.
This repository ALSO carries .github/workflows/review-attested.yml, an older gate that predates
this file (#20, #23, #27). It publishes an `attested` check run and reads NOTHING from here: it
matches the rate-limit notice by regex, counts formal reviews and inline comments on the head sha
through the pulls API, and clears on a `## Review triage` comment. The two agree on the triage
heading (this file's `triage.marker`, the workflow's `^#+ *Review triage` regex) and that is the
only coupling. They answer different questions: `attested` asks 'was a declined review disclosed',
the queue asks 'is there reviewer output newer than the last disposition'. A reviewer that posts
through the comments API (PR-Agent, below) is visible to the queue and invisible to `attested`.
review_markers ARE MEASURED HERE, NOT COPIED. Measured 2026-09-06 over every non-trivial PR in
the history, #14..#28 (twelve PRs; #19, #24, #26 are issues). What CodeRabbit emits here, by PR:
## Walkthrough                          -> #15 #23 #27 #28   (a review ran; the attesting marker)
No actionable comments were generated   -> #28               (clean run; the dotfiles marker
DOES appear here, unlike ts-bridge)
(every one also carries 'rate limited by coderabbit.ai')
## Review skipped                       -> none observed here
#27 carries BOTH: the first push drew the limit notice, a later push drew a walkthrough. That is
the case #19 was filed about and the reason `attested` re-reports on every comment.
Decline rate: 9 of 12 PRs drew the quota notice on at least one push (75 %). Formal reviews with
'Actionable comments posted' exist on #15 #23 #27 #28 only. This is the measurement behind porting
pr-agent.yml alongside this file.
Note the asymmetry that survives this: a CodeRabbit run that files ONLY a formal review with no
walkthrough comment still reads as 'no reviewer output yet'. That is a property of the tool, which
scans comments, and it is why pr-stewardship still asks a human to read the diff.
REBASED ON THE SSOT, November 2026. This is a port, so the SHAPE and the mechanism prose follow
dotfiles/harness/review-attestation.json; the marker VALUES stay local, because they were measured
here and the SSOT's were measured somewhere else. Three things were adopted and one was refused:
adopted   `triage.standing` — who may write the disposition record, which the SSOT added because
a triage comment is what takes a PR out of the queue, so a marker from any commenter
would clear the step a merge is held to. The set matches pr-agent.yml exactly, which
is what makes it a statement about this repo rather than a copy.
adopted   `classification` — the machine-readable severity line, which the SSOT added because a
gradation buried in prose cannot be read back. It is only real if .pr_agent.toml asks
for the exact line, so both changed together.
adopted   the `## Incremental PR Reviewer Guide` marker, a second heading PR-Agent emits.
refused   `exempt.signatures` for release-please. That signature names versions.conf, a file
that does not exist here, and this repo has no release-please: versions are CalVer
stamped from CHANGELOG.md by a human commit. Copying it would add an exemption that
can never legitimately fire, which is an author rule in disguise.
scripts/check-harness.mjs asserts the two couplings that can silently rot: the trusted-association
set against pr-agent.yml, and the classification contract against .pr_agent.toml.

review_markers: No actionable comments were generated in the recent review
reviewers.why: ADVISORY, same disposition as the dotfiles, kubelab and ts-bridge registries: its REVIEW attests, its DECLINE does not refuse. CodeRabbit's quota is a third party's billing state rather than a property of the change, and in this repo the decline is the normal case: 9 of the 12 measured PRs drew 'Review limit reached', so a decline that REFUSED would make the gate red more often than green and teach everyone to ignore it. An advisory decline yields `pending`, the honest answer. `## Review skipped` has not been observed here; it is retained because it is a decline shape CodeRabbit emits on the sibling repos and a decline marker that never matches cannot produce a false 'clear' (only an unmatched REVIEW marker can). LOGINS MATCH WITH TRAILING '[bot]' STRIPPED AND CASE FOLDED: REST reports coderabbitai[bot], GraphQL reports coderabbitai.

PR-Agent (see .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml) runs under GITHUB_TOKEN and publishes through the COMMENTS api, so its reviews never enter reviews[] and a classifier that looked only at reviews would read every PR-Agent-reviewed PR as unattested. The markers are the `review` command's own headings: the full Guide, and the incremental Guide a later push emits. `## PR Code Suggestions` is deliberately NOT here — suggestions are not a review, which is also why auto_improve is off on the automatic path. MARKER PROVENANCE: verified in the sibling ports (kubelab has 215 PR comments carrying '## PR Reviewer Guide' posted by github-actions[bot], dotfiles 172); the incremental heading is the SSOT's, adopted with this rebase. Neither has been observed in this repository: the workflow landed in the same PR as this file, so this entry is still partly a declaration of intent. Until the first Guide lands the queue treats PR-Agent as a reviewer that has not spoken, which is `pending`, not `clear` — the honest answer, and the reason a missing marker is safe: only an unmatched REVIEW marker can produce a false 'clear'. Note that review-attested.yml does NOT count these markers: a PR reviewed only by PR-Agent while CodeRabbit is rate-limited still needs a `## Review triage` comment to turn `attested` green.

triage.standing_why: Who may write the record. A triage comment is what takes a PR out of `dotf pr triage-queue`, so a marker from any commenter would clear the disposition step a merge is held to. These are GitHub author_association values, and the same set the shared PR-Agent job (mlorentedev/ci-workflows pr-agent.yml, called from .github/workflows/pr-agent.yml) trusts before it will run a slash command from a comment — a public repository runs `issue_comment` in the base repo context with secrets available, so the two gates answer the same question and must not drift. scripts/check-harness.mjs compares this set with the caller's concurrency list, which must equal the shared job's; ci-workflows tests that equality for the kit.
triage.why: The heading the pr-review-triage skill records its dispositions under, matched at line start. Declared once here and read back by `dotf pr triage-queue`; review-attested.yml matches the same heading by regex (`^#+ *Review triage`), so a change here must be mirrored there. It is posted even when there was nothing to dispose of: 'CI green, no review findings' is a disposition, and leaving it unwritten is indistinguishable from nobody having looked. Measured here: #15 #22 #25 #27 #28 carry one.

classification.why: A finding's class is read from a whole line equal to prefix + class, never parsed out of prose: the SSOT measured PR-Agent writing the gradation as a header suffix, as the first word of the body, and sometimes not at all. A finding with no such line, or with two that disagree, is unclassified and goes to a human. `.pr_agent.toml` asks for exactly these lines in `extra_instructions`, and scripts/check-harness.mjs fails if the two drift apart. `reviewers` names who is asked for the line: PR-Agent (github-actions) only, because CodeRabbit writes its own severity format and every one of its findings would read as unclassified. Naming the class is not a severity claim — REAL means a concrete trace was given, not that the finding is important.

escape.label: merged-unreviewed
escape.why: Both are required, never one. Proceeding on an unreviewed PR is allowed; proceeding SILENTLY is not. The label plus the section is what forces the disclosure into the durable record instead of a chat message. The label does not exist in this repository yet (labels checked 2026-09-06: only GitHub's defaults); it is created by hand the first time it is needed, which is also the first time anyone has to decide to use it.

exempt.$comment: No signature is exempt, and the mechanism is still declared because an empty list and an undefined one are different statements. Matching is by DIFF SIGNATURE — every changed file must appear in `files`, and the match is SET EQUALITY in both directions: one extra file and the exemption stops applying, one declared file not touched and it stops applying just as surely. Never by author or branch, because neither is something the change carries. This repository has no release-please: versions are CalVer stamped into the footer by src/data/version.ts from the first `## vYYYYMMDD` heading in CHANGELOG.md, in a commit a human writes, so every PR is a change someone authored and every one is reviewed. The SSOT's release-please signature is deliberately not ported — it names versions.conf, which does not exist here, so it could never fire. Declaring an exemption without a measured diff signature would be an author rule in disguise.
